Шевелись, Плотва!Для начала, хотелось бы начать с плюсов и минусов игры:Плюсы:● Огромный мир, наполненный разнообразным уникальным контентом.● Большое количество стилистически выверенных и озвученных диалогов.● Нелинейный сюжет (что в принципе логично для жанра RPG).● Удивительная атмосфера.● Интересная и богатая история мира и персонажей.Минусы:● Слабый искусственный интеллект.Я, как любитель фэнтези и фанат книжной вселенной Ведьмака (автор Анджей Сапковский), никак не мог пропустить 3-ю часть преключений Геральта из Ривии.В отличие от большинства RPG, игра делала акцент не на зачистке подземелий, охоте на драконов и создании собственного приключения, а на том, чтобы провести игрока через детективную историю, за которой интересно следить. В центре истории не абстрактный "Избранный", которого игрок наполняет характером и способностями по своему усмотрению, а самостоятельный, харизматичный ведьмак Геральт. Возможно, это самая сильная сторона всей серии — у каждого игрока получается свой ведьмак, но Геральтом он от этого быть не перестает. В каком-то смысле, Геральт даже не главный герой собственной игры — большинство глобальных проблем мира «Ведьмака» связаны с Цири, и именно она должна спасти его от конца света. Избранная в этой истории — именно потерянная Цири, а ищущий ее Геральт в просто решает насущные проблемы и работает ногами. В этом и кроется секрет обаяния и живости этого мира и его героев — каждый персонаж имеет в нем свое место и остается в своей роли до конца.Обширная карта насыщена интересными местами и с любовью проработанными, оригинальными заданиями, которые рассказывают собственные небольшие истории. Очень часто Геральт просто оказывается свидетелем чужой трагедии.Что касается боевой системы, CD Projekt RED идеально подгадала баланс между глубиной и простотой в освоении. Игра берет не сложным, полным напряжения и страданий игровым процессом, а духом приключения, путешествия великого воина, для которого убийство монстров не подвиг, а рутина, способ заработать на хлеб, кров и новую броню.Первые месяцы они регулярно выпускали бесплатные DLC с костюмами для персонажей, броней для Геральта и небольшими, но качественными квестами. Просто потому, что могли. И это не могло не радовать, ведь для меня регулярные патчи становились настоящим событием, ведь в них часто были не только исправления, но и целые новые функции вроде сундуков-схронов и сортировки предметов в инвентаре, а к выходу «Крови и вина» вышел патч, практически полностью переосмысливший все игровые меню.Кратенько о платные аддонах:«Каменные сердца» представляют собой сравнительно небольшой аддон, который открывает несколько новых локаций в окрестностях Новиграда и добавляет небольшую историю примерно на 10 часов геймплея. Это очень личное приключение, в котором Геральт едва ли не впервые старается не ради денег или близких людей, а ради самого себя.«Кровь и вино» это огромный аддон, события которого происходят в Туссенте, солнечном и процветающем регионе, в котором производят лучшее в мире вино. Проходить «Кровь и вино» желательно после основного сюжета, так как именно там, в Туссенте, ведьмак наконец находит душевный покой.У CD Projekt RED получилось что-то невероятное — самый настоящий высокобюджетный фэнтези-блокбастер, который своей четкой сбалансированностью напоминает фильмы по комиксам Marvel. «Ведьмак 3» — это та игра, с которой просто необходимо познакомиться.10 Ведьмаков из 10.

AT THE CURRENT STATE I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME  Currently the game is riddled with bugs and optimization issues and in my opinion should've been delayed a lot longer.  NOTE: Current actual playtime as of writing is 16hrs, steam playtime is 74min since I've refunded the game here and gotten it on GOG All the problems aside, this is a pretty mediocre game set in a beautifully crafted world. The story is in a way unique but nothing special, it feels unfinished which can be seen in the very intro of the game with how lackluster and weak the lifepath options really are. The "RPG" elements and dialog choices really feel unfinished and are just "slapped on" so that it can be called an RPG. Combat/gunplay/melee feels okay but compared to something like Destiny 2 or Borderlands 3 it doesn't come even CLOSE! Melee was the most fun I've had in combat.Crafting in general feels very useless since the guns you find/buy can and usually are better.Driving feels unresponsive and clunky, which I assume can and hope get fixed. NOW ONE THE BIGGEST PROBLEMS FOR ME  which I found to be very immersion breaking is the AI. Combat AI, driving AI, pedestrian AI...just AI in this game in general is so  BAD Pedestrians feel like braindead zombies just walking around and barley reacting to the environment, the only thing I noticed they do is that they all just crouch down in the same "scared" animation when someone starts shooting. IT DOESN'T EVEN COME CLOSE to games like GTA and RDR2 in that regard. I'm not kidding when I say that GTA San Andreas had better AI than this game. It's a real damn shame...this game world has so much potential since the environment itself has been built incredibly well and the most fun I've got out of this game was from exploration which was in a way diminished by an incredibly dumb AI that took all the immersion out of it. Overall Score for this game is: 6/10 ...given more time to polish the game it would've been easily an 8/10

20 часов, но избрав такой путь вы очень сильно пожалеете дойдя до финала.После прохождения сюжетных заданий персонажи принимавшие в них участие частенько будут говорить вам погулять пару дней и подождать звонка от них, т.к им нужно решить свои проблемы или просто отдохнуть, не пренебрегайте этой возможностью, таким образом разработчики мягко советуют вам обратить свое внимание на дополнительные квесты и активности в игре.Второстепенные задания и прочие активностиВ данном аспекте игры спрятана очень большая часть не менее великолепных квестов чем в основном сюжете, все ваши новоприобретенные по сюжету знакомые будут раскрыты именно в этих заданиях, более того, после прохождения некоторых дополнительных заданий вам откроются новые возможности при прохождении дальнейшего сюжета, а именно две новые концовки.Так же Night City под завязку забит более мелкими активностями, вроде знакомых нам до боли знаков вопроса или заданий в которых мы можем помочь полиции разобраться с бандами которые вышли из-под контроля.Что касается знаков вопроса, как правило это простенькие задания каждое из которых займет не более чем 20 минут вашего времени, но их тоже не стоит упускать, т.к в них тоже встречаются интересные ситуации.А, что касается помощи полиции - эти задания можно смело пропускать и не тратить на них свое время, если вы остро не нуждаетесь в луте, деньгах или репутации, абсолютно никакого сюжета в них нет.ВариативностьИгра предоставляет множество возможностей для прохождения миссий, станете ли вы размахивать катаной как мастер-самурай или будете скрытно взламывать противников будучи нетранером или решите действовать по старинке вооружившись парой автоматов и гранат, а возможно попытаетесь комбинировать в себе сразу несколько стилей - Просто многие завысили свои фантазии и желания, з-зиа чего на выходе получили совсем не то, чего ожидали. Киберпанк: это игра, сделанная с любовью. Cyberpunk 2077Night City is impenetrably big to begin with. It's only with the help of the breadcrumb-trail mini-map I find my way around. Almost immediately, I meet Jackie, the friend you've seen in the gameplay videos, who begins to guide me around. Depending on which background story you choose for your character - Nomad, Street Kid or Corporate - Jackie can be introduced in various ways.Jackie, like the other characters you'll meet, is well drawn. A lot of effort has gone into how they look, how they move and how they sound. I particularly like how Cyberpunk 2077 moves characters around in dialogue so they're not stuck in one place. It gives the sense character performance has progressed a level. You're also free to move around in dialogue; you're not locked into a dialogue camera angle. Dialogue occurs fluidly (apart from in set scripted moments). Walk up to someone and dialogue choices appear, walk away and they disappear. Think of how much time this will save in the long run, especially when you're whizzing around trying to get things done.It's CD Projekt Red showing its open-world experience. Then there's the car, which you're given early on. You don't need to remember where you parked it because you can call it to you, like Roach in The Witcher 3. The car looks nice, with a pointy front and winged doors, and pumps little jets of fire from the exhaust pipes when you go up a gear.Combat, like the city you arrive in, is also a lot to take in. Really, it's three games in one: shooting, stealth and hacking.Shooting doesn't need much explanation because it works the same as in most other games, albeit with a cover system which doesn't stick you to cover but allows you to crouch-shuffle around. Generally, it feels good - there's clearly a lot of gun geekery going on - with lovely damage numbers popping out of people's heads.Stealth is also familiar. You crouch-walk behind people to take them down, lethally or non-lethally, it's up to you. You can hide bodies in nearby containers, or if your enemy is standing next to a container to begin with, you can take-down-n-stash in one nifty move. A slight differentiation comes in with the tech you can employ (and implant). This allows you to scan environments and mark enemies, allowing you to keep track of where they are, even behind objects, and which way they're facing. If they spot you, an alertness gauge begins to fill so you have a bit of time to try and hide again.Consider all of the combat approaches and related abilities, and all of the Cyberware upgrades and perks, and you begin to see what I'm getting at: it's both a lot to take in and a giddying amount of potential.But Cyberpunk isn't all about combat. Your attribute scores (and your background) also contribute to unlocking special dialogue options, which appear with little icons next to them. One appears for me while talking to a lady called Judy Alvarez, who's about to introduce me to Braindances (which I talk about below). I have a high Technical Ability so I'm able to ask her about the tech she's running in her computer den. We hit it off and she warms to me, and says come visit her again.Cyberpunk 2077 is a game about being in a world and gradually colouring it in, populating a map with people you meet and the places as you meet them. It's a playground rife with opportunity and a playground. It's a game about deciding who you want to be.

Best aspects:Firstly the story and side missions are amazing; I personally find it hard to get into the stories of games, but the story of cyberpunk is very good. The characters and acting definitely carry it, and I often found myself willingly participating in additional dialogue with characters, which I never do in video games. The side missions are all really high quality, and never feel like an after thought. Side missions often take part in there own unique areas / buildings, and never feel repetitive. The extra side content is also very fun. Other than side missions there are two types of side content in the game: gigs and random crime events. Gigs are like mini side missions which are more like more standard open world game side missions but shorter, for example killing a guy, or rescuing someone. These sound boring, but they are actually quite diverse, and often have unique characters and areas to explore. Crime events are basically just fun little things to do while exploring, like killing some thugs, or stopping an assault. These are nothing to write home about, but they make the world feel more lively and make the open world more fun to explore. Obviously the most impressive aspect of cyberpunk, and probably why it took so long to make, is the open world. The first time I stepped into night city I was blown away. It's by far, the most impressive open world in a video game ever. The buildings are so detailed and everything has so much depth. You can go inside so many different buildings and shops it's honestly crazy, and I have no clue how the game is only 60 gigs. Even parts of the city I've visited multiple times feels new every time I visit them, just cause of the insane amount of detail. You honestly have to play the game yourself to understand, and maybe i'm a bit bias, as I love the cyberpunk aesthetic, but in my opinion, night city is years ahead of any other open world, I can't stress that enough.Good aspects:An aspect of cyberpunk I like is the character customisation. The cosmetic customisation is pretty good, nothing amazing, but it's good enough. They're seems to be a lot of different clothing items and armour, and I'm 50 hours in, and still finding loads of new clothing items I haven't seen yet at every shop. I've seen people complain that their character didn't look how they wanted them to, cause they were just equipping stuff with the best stats; this is a stupid criticism and applies to literally any game with armor customisation. My character always looked how I wanted him to, as you can upgrade armor you like, and you can sell armor you looted, and replace it with better looking armor from a shop.Skills progression is pretty good in this game, and not as complicated as people say. There are three forms of skills in this game. Firstly there's your character perks / attributes. which are like skyrim's system mixed with fallout's. There are 5 attributes which you can improve with perk points you get from leveling up. Each attribute has 3 skills which level up as you play the game, similair to skyrim, how sneaking improves your stealth skill, and using certain weapon types improves the skills associated with that weapon type. Then each skill has a load of perks, which you need perk points to acquire, which you get from improving your skills. The perks can be quite interesting, and they give the player lots of different options for character builds. The second type of skills progression is your cyberware. You have to buy upgrades to your cyberware and these can range from being able to slowdown time when you get noticed (metal gear style), to mantis blades, to standard stat improvements. Cyberware is pretty interesting and fun, and gives more opportunity to making interesting builds. the final type of skills is your cyberdeck. You can buy hacks for your cyberdeck which are like non-passive skills and basically cyber magic, but they can help create more interesting character builds, or they cane be completly ignored, if you don't want to play a netrunner build.Another aspect of cyberpunk I enjoyed is the combat. There's not much to say here really, guns feel good and the range of builds would definitely make combat feel different on different characters. They're are loads of guns and melee weapons, and they all feel unique.The let downs:The only genuinely bad aspect of cyberpunk, and definitely my biggest disappointment is the AI (combat AI is ok tho). A lot of people have been complaining that police just spawn behind you, and won't chase you in cars if you commit crimes, but the game doesn't actually give you a reason to commit crimes, so I don't mind this, as it's not a huge part of the game, unlike RDR2 where you actually had motive to break the law. My main issues are with the NPCs.  It's not a huge issue in all honesty, It's just quite immersion breaking when the only reaction NPCs have to you shooting in public is them just ducking with their hands over their heads, especially when there's ten NPCs just ducking all in the same position. I have a feeling this is a bug, as they can stay in this pose for wayyy too long, and it doesn't feel right. I'd just like to say, I understand why they're AI is so simple. The game is already extremely CPU intensive, and if every NPC had complex AI, it just wouldn't be possible to run the game with a good population density.Before I get into the bugs and performance I'm just gonna list some nitpicks I have. Firstly the game gives you too many side missions automatically without you choosing to accept them, and the journal becomes insanely cluttered after only a few hours. Whenever you get close to a side activity you receive a call, from one of the characters, and considering there's a side activity on basically every street, it gets kind of annoying. Lastly, the game doesn't let you change your base character appearance once you've created them.Ok, so let's talk about the bugs and performance. Let me start by saying, on PC atleast, the game is not that buggy. I've had no crashes, I've had like 2 bugs that required be to restart the game or load a save, one of them was my controller stopped working and the other was that the FOV was stuck at like 70, so nothing major, and finally I've had a few visual bugs, but nothing compared to a game like fallout or skyrim. So the game is buggy, but no more buggy than any other game like this at launch. Performance on the other hand, is a whole separate issue. My specs are: RTX 2080ti (small overclock), ryzen 3700x (overclocked to 4.5ghz on all cores), 16gb ram and the game is installed on an SSD. Now just for a reference I play RDR2 at 1440p ultra settings and I get 70 to 90fps. when playing cyberpunk my FPS drops bellow 60 when playing at 1080p low settings. Now in most areas, the game runs perfectly, and I can play 1440p with no dlss ultra settings with rtx off. but there's certain areas, mainly the markets, where my fps drops as low as 50. This clearly isn't to do with my GPU as no matter what settings or resolution I'm playing at, my fps always drops to about 50, so it's probably to do with my cpu. I have an 8 core 16 thread top of the line cpu, with a fat overclock (not to flex), I dread to think what this game would play like on a lower end CPU. Ray tracing performance is also terrible, I can't play 1080p with RTX on at a stable 60fps even with DLSS set to quality. Hopefully they'll improve this but, don't expect to be playing this game smoothly with RTX on. CDPR has really pissed me off because of this, they blatently mislead customers, with their recomended specs, cus good luck playing this on a 1060 with a quad core cpu. I'm pretty sure they will improve the performance, but if your on a lower end system, wait before you buy the game.My rating:not taking performance and bugs into account, I'd give the game a 8.75 out of 10, but i'd definitely suggest waiting for performance improvements before buying.

牺牲了之前900+的赞，改为好评。7/10 不够满意，但足以好评如果你是为了赛博朋克版gta来的，肯定会非常失望，2077是一款披着赛博朋克皮的传统rpg。无论蠢驴之前在开放世界、开放玩法上宣传了多少，在开放世界的设计上距离R星和育碧都还有一定的距离，举个例子，行人npc对玩家行为的反应就不是一个级别，希望作为技术储备，能在后续作品中有所提高。但作为rpg来看，2077做得还是挺不错的，单说题材就挺新颖，废土rpg倒是不少，赛博朋克rpg我还真是第一次见，数值的控制还算理想，双等级制鼓励玩家进行探索，而不是通过等级压制等方式强迫玩家去完成支线。2077最大的问题还是，想做的东西太多了，然而心有余而力不足，最后被迫砍掉很多设定，比如出身对剧情的影响（只有前30分钟不大一样），宣传时所说的网状叙事结构，义体对玩法的影响（大部分义体只是属性，改变玩法的义体少之又少，最后变成了双装备制），完全可以无视的服装外观（奇幻题材rpg我可以属性至上，现代和未来题材我真的不想为了属性穿得奇奇怪怪，更别提还不能整容了），和各街头势力的关系（这个真的要学学天外世界）......这些问题都与游戏底层系统设计强相关，几乎不可能在后续更新和dlc中进行修改，只能期待续作中蠢驴能注意到这些问题了。无论如何，2077都是值得一玩的作品，但离神作还有很长的路要走。

I have played almost all the way through the game, i am mostly just finishing off the few last side quests and purchasing the last Vehicles (thanks to gamer OCD) before jumping into the final Chapter.As you can see i have spent 104 hours in the game and of that i would assume ~1-3 hours only was paused as i only played when i had a decent chunk of time.My initial review was NEGATIVE now it is POSITIVE, why?Because it is an excellent game - maybe not quite the groundbreaking revolution in gaming we were led to believe but still a stunning experience.The story flows well and the little Easter Eggs and narrative nuggets that pop up through random side-quests makes completing them interesting. The people are interesting, the city is interesting and i feel i have only scratched the surface with it - just jumping up random buildings can lead to surprises and i would love to dedicate the time to it.The city IS amazing, different Sectors FEEL different and the ebb-and-flow of the background pedestrians is realistic enough for me to be able to guess the time just by walking down the street.I would have liked a Faction-Reputation system though because apparently everyone knows who i am but Scavs and Tyger Claws (both of whom i kill on sight) still do not come hunting for me!Combat is nothing revolutionary. There are plenty of options for how you want to go about your combat but by mid-playthrough i was generally following my pattern of Cyberpsychosis Quickhack, Contagion Quickhack on the all-out brawl, snipe any serious danger and then go in with tech Rifle and SMG.To be honest i would play on one of the harder difficulties next time just to make combat more challenging because by this stage of the game (level 47 and 50 Street Cred) there are rarely any combats that come close to worrying me.As for the RPG element. I feel that i owned my V, that she became 'her own person'. In some ways i feel she had more of her own personality shine through than Geralt did in The Witcher 3 who was a body we 'inhabited'Still, the skill trees were fairly bland IMHO and i currently have a few Level and Perk points unused because the skill trees are not 'begging' to be developed further.BUGS?I am part of the PC Master Race. Running a desktop and although it is nothing near top of the line it is still EASILY handling the game's demands. I can honestly say i had as many visual bugs (clipping issues and random graphic glitches) as i did in TW3 and when i bought TW3 it had been out for YEARS.I have had 1 CTD and that was when i did something stupid and then tried to load mid-stupid.What i Dislike DRIVING is just plain annoying and needs to be fixed. Trying to do it with the keyboard is frustrating and the best driving i have ever managed still make my V look drunk.The KEYMAPPING LIMITATIONS - grow up guys, it is the year 2021 and you are still locking most non-WASD options (see my initial review).Overall I am happy with the amount i paid for CP2077, especially after getting TW3 with all expansions for $20. I will happily play this game again when i am done with a Corpo Netrunner build on a much higher difficulty level - i think i will wait until the major patch is done though just to see what it brings.To me CP2077 plays like what Deus Ex HR/HE could have been... the Quickhacking especially is amazing and there have been entire missions i have been able to complete from outside the building as i hacked my way through a chain of cameras.I also feel that there is SO much in 2077 that is a placeholder for more DLC and stories - i do not believe the cut content BS for one second, the launch issues alone make that highly improbable. I think there are so many stories coming and i WANT to play them.*** INITIAL REVIEW ***Welcome to the cyber future... where the most elite and powerful cyberforces known to humanity are ruled over by their WASD overlords. Where remapping the arrow-keys is a lost art of techno-sorceryCannot rebind the Up/Down arrow for V... in 2020. Or remap the Enter key either (it defaults to Right Shift)Maybe anything except WASD is illegal in Poland?

终于全成就了，过来写个评测如果你正在阅读这篇评测，并且还在犹豫要不要购买这款游戏的话，那么我的答案是 不。  1.作为一款剧情向开放世界游戏，剧情肯定是非常重要的一环。简单说一下《赛博朋克2077》的剧情。剧情总体来说我要给个中评，挺正常的一剧情，没什么雷点也没什么神转折。但是就它的篇幅来说，我要给个差评。如果你全力推主线的话，你就会发现这款游戏的主线真的是短的不能再短了，差不多一天左右就能迎来结局了，估摸着可能在14小时左右的游玩体验——这还算上了听满全部的对话，实际真正的游戏体验时间还会更少。这对于一款售价近300R的游戏来说显然是非常不划算的。当然还会有穿插在主线中的各种支线，看似茫茫多，实则真正有内容的只有帕南、朱迪、克里和瑞弗的支线，算上这些可能会将游戏的时间提升到30小时左右？至于为什么我没把其他的支线算上，原因是重复度过高，无非是让你去某个地方杀个人、调查一下、偷个东西，然后屁颠屁颠跑过去交货当个打工人，实在是有些无聊，开放世界的劫匪就更是如此了，枯燥无味的打钱过程。不过对于这款游戏的剧情完成度，我一定会给个好评。大量的对话分支以及数不清的分离芯片，很好的补全了剧情的完整度和世界观，可能这就是CDPR想要追求的沉浸式体验吧。  2.我一开始是奔着智能武器来玩这款游戏的，毕竟谁不喜欢不用瞄准就能随便开枪乱杀呢。可是越玩就越发现智能武器是有极限的，所以我换了技术武器。你说你玩动能武器？那请您受我一拜。什么？你说你玩的是冰暴？哦，那没事了。枪械平衡性，这游戏解禁到现在最大的问题。智能武器确实很爽，但是奈不住他刮痧啊，勉强凑合的只有一把阿修罗，刮痧还不是智能武器的最大问题。室内不宜发挥、诡异的乱锁定、目标距离远锁定不上，这些才是智能武器的最大问题。动能武器这边则是纯粹的eng刮，常规的动能武器包括了大部分的冲锋枪、突击步枪、手枪、轻机枪，简直就是灾难，比起智能武器还要瞄准和压枪，更难受了。至于技术武器这边，不说了，能穿墙就是人上人。综上所述，智能武器里推荐阿修罗，动能武器推荐冰暴，推荐大部分的技术武器以及左轮手枪、精准步枪、霰弹枪。强烈推荐M-179E阿喀琉斯，本身是技术武器的同时兼顾了远程蓄力当狙用，近战突突是霰弹的多功能性，而且单个弹匣载弹量高，弹匣换弹，不要太爽。 最后提一下近战：我tm砍爆，砍就完事了。  3.载具自由度也是一个头疼的问题，都2077年了还是之能开地上跑的车，我好难啊。那些个浮空车，机甲高达装甲车什么的，就不能给V整一个吗？吗？吗？ 说真的，CDPR要是能让我开上机甲，这篇评测不管别的我都要给好评。  4.作为一个有明显赶工痕迹的半成品，BUG数不过来也在预料之中。如果说游戏性不强还能够接受的话，那么糟糕的优化和大量未修复的bug则是压死大部分玩家的最后一根稻草。  综上所述，我并不推荐还在犹豫的玩家原价购入《赛博朋克2077》这款游戏，等到打折再入手会是更好的选择。如果让我购买第二份《赛博朋克2077》的话，我会选择CDPR发售第一或者第二个大型DLC的时候，毕竟CDPR的大型DLC做的是真的好，希望《赛博朋克2077》的DLC也能够有《巫师3》的DLC那么精致。最后我想说我为什么会给差评。仅仅是因为它没有达到我的预期罢了。那么大的宣发力度，吊足了我的胃口，让我等了好久，玩到最后感觉也就是个标准的3A。跳票并不是什么关键问题，关键是没有那种让人眼前一亮的感觉。它没有让我觉得：哇 这个东西好帅，这个系统设计的真好，这个剧情怎么怎么好。给我更多的感觉是我在玩一款《GTA》和《巫师》杂交的产物。希望DLC能够让我大吃一惊吧。

Cyberpunk 2077 isn't perfect, but it is ambitious. It marries a gripping story with a huge open world absolutely dripping with atmosphere; one in which, after 90 hours of gameplay, I still feel like I've only scratched its surface. Even now I'm itching to jump back in and complete yet more side jobs, not only because they're enjoyable, but also just in case they offer V more options when it comes to ending their story. I'm even contemplating starting over anew to change the outcome of some events with the benefit of hindsight. If you were expecting a light-hearted affair full of futuristic hijinks then you might not find what you want here – though it does let its hair down every once in a while. Instead, what Cyberpunk 2077 delivers is a surprisingly serious story that's genuinely touching at times, with gameplay that lets you be in charge of your destiny. If you want your experience in Night City to be as polished as possible, perhaps hold back until a patch or two has landed to iron out some kinks, but you'll definitely want to visit soon. Phenomenal, that's what Cyberpunk 2077 is.

TL;DR..This game has me so conflicted. My initial review was negative and while I stand by my initial comments, further playing has changed the overall review. Its good, its great, its fantastic but just about all interactions with the game range from bad to terrible.The Good:The city.. is just fantastic. It feels vibrant, alive and just massive. In around 10 hours of playing I'm not even sure I've been in half of the regions. Going up to random doors sometimes says Locked as though it may become accessible eventually. The city blocks are huge but those of us who dislike driving usually have shortcuts. There are so many things going on that make you want to go and see what it is... a detour from the side quest that is a detour from the main quest which is itself a detour from exploring. It feels like you could find thousands of hours of game play just by going for a walk. Its grimy, filthy and crowded.The UI is what you'd expect in a sci-fi fantasy rpg and works well but some scaling options would be nice. I was pleasantly surprised by the subtitles and how other languages were handled. The story is surprisingly interesting & engaging and while I thought I'd seen a fair bit in early teasers I was pleased to find those were all in early 'hand-holding' parts of the game. The named NPCs are varied and have depth.  Background NPCs are varied, interesting and plentiful. Its nice to see the downtrodden drifting around with a suitably lifeless looking walk.The quests are varied and interesting with a celebrity appearance or two. While there are only a limited number of quest types you can really do (steal, retrieve, kill, rescue, deliver etc) they do feel different enough that they don't feel tedious or repetitive and serve to send you around the map quite nicely.The game has fast travel stations which might seem immersion breaking but does really help getting around.The sound is good although my music is muted so I cant comment on that. Path-finding & AI movement looks natural and more than realistic enough. The graphics are impressive and while graphics are less important to me than most other parts of the game they can enhance or ruin a game. The city looks real and I honestly didn't see any signs of seams or tiling.Cyberpunk 2077 makes great use of ray-tracing while not making every surface look stupidly shiny so a big congratulations for that.The Bad:I noticed a few glitches like NPCs & vehicles sometimes spawning in 3 metres away or moving through walls or minor visual bugs like floating chopsticks or guns in heads but I feel like these are noticeable because they are so infrequent. Its a little too easy to get on someones bad side. While wearing no faction specific outfit sometimes people start shooting just because you walked past and its nearly impossible to not commit crimes while crossing the city. These wouldn't be so bad if it didn't take so long to leave 'combat'. Jobs or side quests keep popping up to the point where the Journal felt cluttered and that's not even counting those other events that keep popping up. I love it I really do but it feels like I'm getting swamped when I'm still just wanting to explore and learn my way around. The combat is just bad. I skip the combat whenever I can but having to fire 80 or more bullets into someone's head from a metre away to kill them is a bit much and takes too long. I'd hate to see what its like in Hard mode. The rail shooter parts are just rail shooters and need to die but luckily there hasn't been many so far. The tutorials & intro parts of the game take too long and yet some game mechanics like hacking could be explained better.The Ugly: The controls. OMG the controls suck. Some controls cant be reassigned. Aside from the rebinding issues most interaction with the game is just awful. Controls are inconsistent with 6 different keys all being used to close or confirm different things. Mouse movement in menus is really sluggish with no way to alter it. Vehicle steering is too binary, with a slight tap causing your car to swerve violently. Moving around feels like you are Xmen's Juggernaut. Scanning mode can be push-to-use or toggled but why not weapon zoom? Talking to NPCs is laggy and yet timed dialog (QTEs) so short and there is no autorun. Its a massive city in an RPG so why is there no autorun? The only way to holster a weapon is using an option wheel at the most annoying angle. While control issues such as these might seem minor, they make playing the game painfully difficult and yet are so easily fixed. Its quite clear to me that CDPR designed the game with controllers in mind and just gave keyboard & mouse control the minimum effort. ThNotes:In one of the early videos showing game-play footage I noticed that quite a few of the NPCs had the same gait. I was pleased to see it had improved a lot although you do notice similarities like Guy Clutching Arm, every 'large' dude or kid walking like a beefcake.Earlier footage showed how billboards would show things for your character however this didn't seem to happen as far as I noticed. Its entirely possible I didn't notice it (in which case well done CDPR) or its going to be added at a later date but I thought it needed mentioning.My PC is is well above the recommended specs and yet the game runs fairly slowly 27/80fps with RTX on/off at 1440p (35/85fps with the 09/12/20 drivers).Summary: I love CP2077 but the things wrong with the game are just so bad for someone like me. It doesn't matter how nice food is if you can't eat it.---===---First review (at 1 hour of game-play):Controls: garbage, key-binds are broken, its a console game with terrible kbd+mouse settings. some of the settings just don't work or are missing. In 2020 they can't even get game controls working, amateur hour. Controls are a mess, like you're doing QTEs or playing "find the random key".Graphics: not badSound: not badGame-play: Only action so far has been a garbage rail shooter.The story: Interesting but I've known him for 5 minutes and I already hope Jackie dies soon.The actual game... so far i'm seriously unimpressed. It feels clunky, like you're running around wearing a power armour suit. Its too early to say if its a good game but first impressions aren't great.

I really liked this game at first, until I started to realize that the only thing keeping me interested in the game was the narrative. İlk başta Coronado City olarak Richard Night isimli iş adamı tarafından inşa edilen ve Richard Night'ın ölümüden sonra belediye meclisi tarafından anısına Night City  ismini almıştır. Night City  toplamda altı bölgeye bölünmüş durumda. Her bir bölgeyi farklı çeteler kontrol ediyor. Her bölgede yapılabilecek tonla aktivite ve yan görev ile dolu. Oyun içinde şehir yaşadığını hissettiriyor oyuncuya. İşi aldıkları kişi olan Dexter Deshawn bu çipi ölümsüzlüğün çipi olarak tanımalamaktadır. İkili Arasaka kulesine başarıyla girip Yorinobu Arasaka'dan çipi çalmayı başarmıştır fakat bir yandan Arasaka şirketinin sahibi ve ailenin başı olan Saburo Arasaka'nın oğlu Yorinobu Arasaka tarafından öldürülmesine  şahit olmuştur. Bu sırada gelişen olaylar sonrasında ikili zor bir şekilde Arasaka kulesinden kaçmayı başarır fakat kısa bir süre sonra kaçış sırasında yaralanan Jackie  ölür. Bu sırada çipin kutusu kuleden kaçarken hasar gördüğü için V kendine takmak zorunda kalmıştır. V çipi kendine taktıktan sonra Dexter ile buluşmaya gider ve Dexter ihanet eder ve bizi kafamızdan vurur.  Çöplükte uyanıp Saburo Arasaka' nın koruması olan Goro Takemura bizi kurtardıktan sonra nasıl ölmediğimizi anlamaya çalışırken gerçek ise Night City'nin asi, yetenekli bir zamanlar Samurai grubunun solisti ve Keanu Reeves abimizin canlandırdığı Johnny Silverhand'in geri dönüşüdür. Corvo for life ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥...Updated review after actually putting hours into the game, when CP2077 first released I fell in love immediately with the world. What I didn't love were the technical short comings. So much wasted potential even still to this day. We could have had way more verticallity, flying vehicles for transportation, tram systems, taxi systems that actually worked, more in door environments available to explore. Weapon variety, smart rockets/missiles, mines, EMP, the list could go on forever. Movement reminds me a lot of a crytech game, specifically Star Citizen which is fine for me but I could see it feeling stiff and janky for those not use to it. I was most disappointed with the implementation of ray traced shadows and lighting in the beginning. Contact shadows, source shadows, player reflection. It was all just off until this latest patch arrived. The ray traced everything is now amazing! I mean, some of the best implementation I've seen to date. The lore is great, I wish they would have had more branching stories for new character play throughs but I love what is here, I'm very happy CDPR are still working their hearts away at this game. It's a love/hate relationship I'm willing to keep in my life forever like family. My love for it will always supersede my frustrations with it. What is there not to love about a cyber punk world. CP2077 will always hold a special place in my heart far after I complete everything there is to do. Thanks for being great CDPR

EDIT: Final verdict: 5/10.This game is beyond hopeless, patch 1.1 destroyed whatever faith I had left. It's a ♥♥♥♥ game, dumb gameplay, bad graphics, bad performance, virtually no ai. NEVER pre-ordering from CD again.Original:Cyberpunk 2076, is it good???; No. and yes,... here is why. First of yes the main story is fun, if you enjoy a good on rails story, yes fun to play, there is sadly no RPG to be found. If you like rich open worlds or RPG's than this ain't it chief. Let's go over some quotes with promises and than the FACTS first. Fanboys don't read, or pretend it's an Ubisoft game or it might hurt your feelings.CD: "Coming when it's ready"This game is not ready at all, from the piss poor performance to the countless bugs that people encounter. But also not even from a gameplay perspective. This game needed at least 4 more years.CD: "It doesn't matter if you are dead, as long as you are doing it in style"Really??? Why can't I customize my character than??? There is absolutely no emphasis on fashion and style at all, the lack of a transmog system results in your character looking like a clown most of the time. There is almost no customization to be found in this game for being an open world game, you can't even CHANGE YOUR FREAKING HAIRSTYLE.CD: "Each NPC has their own handcrafted routine"I'm even hesitant to call the NPC behavior AI, since stupidly walking from point A to B with the fluidity of a lego stopmotion figure, only to vanish and respawn a few meters away has nothing to do with "intelligence" or a "handcrafted routine". There is no reaction to anything you do, everything feels static and unrealisitic.CD: "The game runs surprisingly well on last gen consoles"This claim about game performance is disputed, see Digital Foundry.CD: "Braindance is a pretty big part of the Cyberpunk universe"Braindance is absolutely nowhere to be seen outside of scripted mission in this game. Than there is lifepaths...... Aside from a meaningless dialogue option every 2 hours and some minor quest differences, lifepaths feel completely meaningless.THE REST OF THE REVIEWAlright so what about this big lively city to explore, where npc's have "handcrafted" routines... "The most realistic open-world to date".... Well, they quickly changed their Twitter bio from: "the role-playing game of the dark future" to > "an open-world action-adventure story", and I can see why, there is no role-playing in this game outside of scripted encounters and the open-world is worse than GTA3 no offense. But why? Here some facts;There is NO driving AI. None. This is also the reason there are no police chases and all story chases are scripted. You can test this by parking your car on a 3 lane highway, they won't go around you because they literally can't. Police just spawns inside you because of lack of ai, also no driving chases.The open-world is dead.There are no interactions, the npc are dumber than in Red Dead 2, that sad actually, Red Dead 2 offers much more roleplay than this "rp-focused" game. You cannot talk at all and they all behave EXACTLY the same. Try stopping a lot of vehicles, throw a grenade and see how they instantly all react the same with the same animations etc. There is no sense of progression.This Borderlands looter-shooter style doesn't work for this game. All these talents trees are hugely uninteresting and only cause menu clutter. The levels don't mean anything and this results in enemies being bullet sponges. Cyberpunk shoves you onto one path (all of the "backgrounds" are very short and lead to the same path) and establishes all the connections for you without you earning it!You can't change your character's appearance etc..You can't change your character's appearance, or car, or buy apartments/houses! You can't sit, you can't take a drink unless the game wants you to, you can't go shopping, can't get a tattoo, can't buy food from food vendors. No mini games, no interesting activities in the world. You can't do anything that isn't heavily scripted by the game. This isn't an RPG at all.Sad to see that even GTA3 has more (non scripted) roleplay than this 2020 game. The open-world is totally meaningless. Like yes it is fun exploring until it hits you that there is absolutely NOTHING to do and there isn't even driving AI to screw around with. As I said if you like a on-rails story where you choice doesn't matter but where you have the illusion of choice than great, you might enjoy it. But it's absolutely not even close to what they advertised and just a pretty bad game for 2020 standards. The game is honestly the definition of "wide as an ocean and deep as a puddle."

Все NPC в лучшем случае ходят по кругу, а все активности и большинство побочных заданий сводится к убийству, воровству или спасению кого-то. Сделано это даже хуже чем у Ubisoft, а они напомню лучшие д е р ь м о д е л ы современности. Система прокачки это просто убожество, половина навыков это повышение на 5-7% выносливости, здоровья, скорости пердежа и прочего... Езда на авто отвратительна, стрельба посредственная. А система розыска просто ''безупречная'', как только вы нарушите закон у Вас за спиной начнут пачками появляться полицейские, без разницы где вы находитесь, хоть на крыше.. Стоит Вам сесть в машину и проехать метров 300, все полицейские тут же забывают про Вас и всё.. Никаких погонь, копы просто не умеют ездить на авто.. Просто слёзы... Поляки подарили нам прекрасных трёх Ведьмаков, они сделали много хорошего, но как говорится стоит тебе один раз трахнуть козу и всё... CD Project Red трахнули козу, выпустив это убожество. Очень жаль, но не советую никому в это играть.

And so Cyberpunk 2077 comes to an end with 2.0(presumably). The game went from being an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ back in 2020 to something actually very enjoyable. I was the first to ♥♥♥♥ all over it after all the false advertising they did with their live streams talking about features that are (still) nowhere to be found in the game, but CDPR has gained some of my trust back.They could've given up on this game years ago, there are live services that die 1 year after release when they are supposed to last 10, and yet CDPR decided to keep working on this for 3 years after its disastrous launch.The new perk and cyberware systems make build variety actually mean something since perks aren't just % increases anymore. You also need to be more picky with what cyberware you want to use because you'll reach the cap fast once you start installing iconic pieces.It's pointless to whine about how they still haven't added in all the features they promised back before release, the amount of work they would need to accomplish that would require almost a full rewrite of the game, which the engine definitely can't handle.The game looked great back in 2020 and now it's absolutely amazing thanks to path tracing, while also running better than another recent release  (starfield) While the story lacks branching paths, it has plenty of small choices that are reflected afterwards, that's more than another certain game can say for itself   (starfield) There are still bugs unfortunately, but they're considerably less than they were in the 1.6 patch, it's been hard to find enough of them to make another bug compilation even after 70 hours on the 2.0 patch.The acting and animations during dialogs/cutscenes are top notch, I hope they keep the quality at this level for their next releases. Back when the 1.6 patch came out, I recommended it for 30€, but now I'd even go up to 50. Taking in all the details the game has to offer has made me enjoy it more, and also showed me just how lacking in care other studios can be   (bethesda) . I'd like to thank Todd Howard for showing me what a ♥♥♥♥ game looks like, so I could learn to enjoy a good one instead. .

TLDR: While it's an incredible feat in narrative storytelling if you pursue the most fulfilling and engaging quest dialogue, the game lacks in so many directions that this review has left me completely polarized. I insist that you wait to buy this game until CDPR (still) fixes the game unless you are willing to experience a truly dystopian mess of a cyberpunk future.The Good: First, probably an undisputed point- the soundtrack is perfect. I was initially disappointed when first playing the game at launch but once I dove deeper into the OST, I was, in a way, taken aback. It nails a gritty, diverse, and cyberpunk dystopian soundtrack that perfectly exemplifies what Cyberpunk 2077 should have been. Second up, graphics. Something that may come off as a bit objective as the experience significantly depends on the hardware you run it on. In December 10th, 2020, when the game launched, I went through a complete playthrough of the game (almost exclusively doing the main quests, only) on a 1050ti. This was a horrible and daunting mistake. On low with 17-21 fps at any moment, the game looked horrible. My second playthrough was somewhere around July, where I used the cloud streaming service Geforce NOW. The graphics were solid but not anywhere near what maxed would have looked like. Now that I've played through with a 3070 and hardware that can run the game, it looks truly incredible. The glow from the neon lights, the clear and crisp reflections from ray-tracing. It didn't occur to me how good the reflections were until one day as I was walking back to my dorm, I looked down at the road after a rainstorm hit and looked agaze at a large puddle that reflected a unique perspective that I hadn't fully recognized. My third point may be a bit more controversial, but it's an opinion at that. The narrative direction was written and performed in a manner that I've never experienced before. In my first playthrough, I finished the main story jetting through a measly few side quests that left me unsatisfied, albeit, empty. That was a directly intentional design choice as I later fell into thought about the impact of the game. There is no "good outcome" for V, one way or another, he/she will die a painful death. Whether that is fulfilling or empty is part of the narrative design. In my second and third playthroughs, I explored Judy's and Panam's storylines and faced more options in the end, one that left me completely shook. I'm not gonna spoil anything, but if you experienced the Temperance ending, you'll understand the impact of choices that underwent during the storm for Mikoshi. Something I realized, later on, was that my overall feeling towards the game heavily compared that to V's relationship to Johnny. My first playthrough was a rocky relationship where I tried to appeal to Johnny but it never really worked out. They were distant exactly like when the two first met. However, in my second and third playthroughs, V's general relationship with Johnny was drastically better. It felt satisfying in a really damn good way. It perplexes me just how the narrative team was able to deliver a story keen on genuinely leaving an impact on the player simply by the choices made during the significant "main" side quests and the general endings you received from them. The neutral:The cars. I'm a complete fanatic when it comes to arcade driving games like Forza and NFS but the driving in the game is... bad, and that's sugar-coating it. The handling characteristics are just off, likely coming from the tuning from the game engine's processing of general physics. Turning is incoherent, the suspension is completely disgusting. Collusion and AI is just broken. The cars themselves are wonderful- the glossy exterior paints, the real-life exhaust noise, the plush cushioned interiors, and the sci-fi UI within the cars themselves just ooze "cool". Something that bugs me is that there is zero vehicle customization in any spectrum whatsoever. For a game that heavily pushed character customization and quest lineage, a feature I would have expected would have been at least changing vehicle paints and rims. Coming off of customization is leading to character design. While the AI designs can be both stunning and off-putting (grown people morphed into children?), it highlights more the graphical showoff of the game and it's engine that actual customization. When you design your character, I felt extremely limited in actual choices because most, if not all, of the actual customization you do to your character is never actually seen- that is, if you accidentally look into the mirror in the bathroom trying to pick up a medical inhaler for some health. Why would I customize my character in a unique and fashionable sense if I will never intentionally see my character, ever, except in a mirror, when prompted to look into it -- or when I pull up the game menu? It's an odd game design choice, to be frank, even when the character customization (of the body) is extensive in some areas like with the eyes and tattoos and extremely limited when choosing different colors. It's something that can look really cool but is underutilized in such an odd way. The bad:Let's get this out of the way- bugs. It's been the talk of the year in regards to Cyberpunk alongside it's astonishing eye-melting graphics. Throughout my playthroughs, I felt like I never really encountered many bugs. My first playthrough, I felt like I rarely ever encountered any (probably because the game was 20fps on low anyways). Actually, now that I'm thinking back, I recall there being an issue where Judy's door wouldn't open after the incident with Evelyn in her apartment preventing me from progressing in her storyline further. My second playthrough I encountered maybe max 3 instances where my car fell through the world. Some visual oddities but nothing game breaking. My third playthrough was just weird though. The game had gone through maybe 4-5 major patches that intended to fix the game, but I found that it just broke it further. Fixers who tend to usually provide you with side quests and vehicles to purchase just didn't call/text me in any regard after the first 4 hours of playtime. It occurred to me after I tried to get the black Caliburn in the cave after helping Panam get her stuff back. I "time-traveled" many numbers of days before giving up but realizing that after looking at my map, there was only 1 vehicle for purchase. I was tried of using the default car because it was didn't have as much characters as the others so I wanted to buy something else at that point. Much to my despair, I had only gotten 1 "ad" to buy a car in something like 20 hours of playtime. How did CDPR push a bug fix that intended to slow the frequency of fixers calling and sending you text to the point where they don't interact with you at all anymore? Frankly, this was just weird that a bugfix had the intention of fixing a feature that wasn't broken at all only to make the problem worse. I ended up just getting some mods to get some cars so I could at least traverse the map in a vehicle that could drive quickly. Second point, the UI. Holy moly this is a dumpster fire. The UI frequently bugged out or just didn't work at some points. My HUD disappeared multiple times, the menu to upgrade your character froze after using an attribute point. Navigating the menus for crafting and upgrading are nightmares. I did not have a great time using the UI at all, but this is an entirely subjective view as user interface experiences are dependent on the person and because there is never gonna be a UI that will satisfy everyone. Lastly, performance. CB2077 is a literal monster. Don't play on consoles, this game will melt them completely. Get an 3060 or better if you want to run the game with decent graphics with a good (but wildly inconsistent) framerate. Optimization has improved incrementally but it still is not in a good state as it is.

While the technical issues have largely been ironed out, there are still areas where the game can improve, such as with the animations and head tracking during driving. However, the developers have shown a commitment to continuing to improve the game, so it's likely that these issues will also be addressed in future updates.However, what truly makes Cyberpunk 2077 shine is its captivating storyline and immersive world. I've barely had any issues with bugs. A few buggy missions here and there, but nothing game-breaking. The game hasn't crashed on me since the first major patch they put out. The bugs have not been a problem whatsoever, at least in my experience. The game doesn't run particularly well, though. My computer's specs are a bit better than the system requirements, but I can't quite pull 60FPS even on minimum settings. Kind of frustrating.But that's not why I don't recommend this game. I could look past those issues if the core game mechanics were still fun. The reason I don't recommend this game is because it's unfinished, unpolished, and boring. The open world, GTA-esque aspects of this game fall flat, and were done way better in GTA V seven years ago. Night City is mostly lifeless, filled with brain-dead NPC's that barely react to their surroundings. GTA has a world that's fun to explore, drive around in, and cause chaos in. In theory, Night City should be even more engaging and I should want to explore every inch of it. But because it feels so lifeless, and so many parts of the city look exactly the same, the game might as well not even have an open world. The world is just an inconvenience that I have to drive though on my way to the next quest.This is probably a hot take, but aside from dialog choices, Fallout 4 does pretty much everything else this game wanted to do, but better. Fallout 4 has interesting side quests, multiple interesting side characters, an actually fun and worthwhile crafting system, and (somehow) a significantly better and less clunky UI. Cyberpunk 2077 has a somewhat more interesting main quest, though I really don't care enough to actually finish it. Even in terms of crafting a believable, living, breathing world with interesting things to explore, the nuclear wasteland of the Commonwealth is better than Night City.I didn't buy into the hype for this game. I put it on my wishlist a long time ago because I thought it kinda looked interesting, and a friend bought it for me. I never watched the trailers or anything like that, so I didn't really have too many expectations coming in. Nonetheless, this game still disappointed me, and I really don't believe it succeeds at anything it set out to do. It's just not fun. CDPR says they're committed to fixing bugs, but even once they do that, this game will still be a half-baked mess.

I tried giving this game another shot after playing the soul-crushing infamous launch in December 2020.After 2.0...it is just okay. Not a game that redefines anything. Everything still feels flat, and remains a shell of what was promised. Plenty of bugs and glitches remain, with NPCs still aimlessly bouncing off each-other in a vibrant cardboard cut-out of a world. The performance ranges from decent to downright bad (especially in the DLC) on 4070ti and 7 3800X on mid-range settings and performance DLSS with frame gen at 4k (no pathtracing). Side missions, gigs, etc. amount to "Hey V, go here and neutralize X to acquire Y, and I'll call/text you when it's done". I have played through what I would guess is about 1/3 of the main story and find myself bored most of the time. Following behind exposition dumping NPCs, going to places to kill or talk to someone and get rushed along to the next story beat. Relationships with characters seem to form staggeringly fast, and motives for helping them or going for revenge feel artificial and forced. Combat is alright, with the diverse perk trees and the ability to respec at any time allowing for a good degree of variation. Each build however does get repetitive though, and I did find my knife-thrower netrunner character getting stale disappointingly fast. Overall, I would give this game a 5 or 6 out of 10 with DLC included. Maybe with a NVIDIA 6000 series GPU I can play at good performance after some optimization, and learn to power through the chaff to find a good game deep down. Unfortunately for now I would say avoid the game and DLC unless you get it at a unbelievable discount and are willing to give CDPR the benefit of the doubt. For now, I think I will back-burner this game at least another 3 years.

And when I say "a bit," about 90% of my gameplay were just grapple kills. Overall, the guns were okay, the hacking was nice, and melee was awesome. I think the use of tech weapons were also a nice embellishment to combat gameplay. Leveling also felt balanced, but playing on hard mode, didn't feel all that hard. The story, for a video game, was pretty good, but I did want it to be longer. I'd say it's definitely on the better side of video game stories. The characters were probably the best part of the game. The romanceable character side quests were, in my opinion, packed with depth, and the outcomes of these quests nicely impacted the ending in small ways. Many of the other side quests also had a lot of personality. They didn't feel as repetitive as other video game side quests, so I was, for the most part, entertained. The visuals are outright fantastic. If you can run this game on max settings, Night City is quite literally breathtaking. Also, the music adds to the atmosphere, so I have no complaints on that. Some things I wish would've been better were the AI and physics of the game. Underwater physics is lacking, but that's forgivable since about 99% of the gameplay is usually on land. It would've been a nice addition to have to add to the realism, but I'm fine without it. However, one of the few things I despised was the enemy AI combat. When I alerted one enemy in a separated room, it sometimes felt like the entire enemy base knew where I was and what I was doing. Idk, maybe I'm too used to enemy AI from games like Dishonored, but Cyberpunk's AI seemed too rudimentary sometimes. The civilians also seemed a bit on the dull side when it came to the AI. And my god, why do police officers spawn at your location when you're being hunted?One final thing: Why. Am. I. Not. Fully. Naked. When. I'm. Not. Wearing. Clothes?! What's the point of customizing my private area if I can't even see 'em?!All in all, this is a great game and I regret nothing; I'm hoping for better and more updates in the future. CDPR definitely could've benefited if they released it later, but what's done is done. If you're thinking about getting this game, maybe wait a bit? Otherwise, just go for it. So here it is. The most hyped game of 2020.It is the most ambitious game to date? Yes. Is it the best game ever? No.The 1980s was the last time humanity had optimism for the future, but unfortunately the world of CyberPunk ruins that neon imagery with a very grimy 2020s idea of a degenerate dystopia. There seems nothing more ridiculous and nihilistic than robots having sex in a filthy city, for one - but here we are.It's also hard to see Japanese text in a world so full of litter and trash - whereas in it's native Japan the country is exceptionally clean. It's more than a bit jarring... but it's going for a "Blade Runner", "Akira", and laughably an "Idiocracy" vibe so you can't accuse the graphics of not being amazing, and yes, beautiful all the same. Hope you can score yourself one of the latest GPUs though. As a world to explore it's freaking amazing with the level of art and of detail. I tip my hat to the art department!To produce the visuals, the game kicks my GTX1080 in the teeth with some poor FPS to produce the 1080p visuals. The gameplay feels like the DeusEx games with a side of Grand Theft Auto, yet complete with Bethesda Fallout-esque combat with a touch of Far Cry. Being an RPG there is an incredibly deep amount of role-playing with an extensive number perk choices to be had for you to customize - penis-size not withstanding. In fact you can even call yourself male and retrofit your groin with female genitalia or breasts. The game is that progressive!Cyberpunk deliberately stands on the shoulders of AAA titles of yore, and so far in my playthorugh it's shaping up to be pretty epic already. It's a huge step up in open-world gaming, as many gameplay elements from many classic AAA games of the past decade are merged into this cyborg, creating an unmatched singularity of single player world exploration and play experience........or at least it should have. Cyberpunk's gameplay also fails to live up to what it could be. It doesn't equal the sum of it's parts. Once I get beyond the prologue I am swamped with quests from randoms I don't know wanting things I don't care about. Not complaining about the amount of content, only that it's just overwhelming and I can't keep up with the story. Info shards you pick up hide themselves away in confusing inventory AI - disjointing you from the story. You are forced to dig the info out - and most people won't bother. Furthermore there's no real intelligence needed to solve the problems. I feel I can just stumble in cut everyone down, or just go around pushing buttons everywhere to solve the quests. There is no need to really follow any story, read any clues (the inventory UI sees to that), to solve any problems - even on hardest difficulty level. Stealth is there, but unlike Deus Ex, not really worth pursuing except on a few quests. You don't have to kill people, but they set up your player as a criminal from the start, with criminal jobs to do. What's a few dead bodies here and there? There's no point pretending to be Jesus when your player's morality is compromised from the start. Driving is nice, but you could easily skip it and fast-travel too. Many of the GTA-style replayable minigames don't really exist here either. Police chases are non-existant. Stunts around the map don't exist, and where there is a solitary ramp - it goes nowhere. The mini-map is the most annoying thing - as it's not zoomed out enough and you routinely miss your turn-off. Melee combat ala Skyrim is fun - except for the bit where everyone carries guns - so that is ruined too. Punches don't seem to land properly. Boxing matches require you to punch the combatant hundreds of times over while they can one-two you onto the canvas - even after modding your character. There's even a basketball and hoop, but unlike Deus-ex I can't even pick the ball up to try that cliche three-pointer.All these things diminish the gameplay and story. Puts the game into more of the tourist exploration and cut-scene entertainment category - which is fine for a particular kind of player. To me it felt like a chore just travelling around the place from one quest to the next - and while the scenery is certainly impressive - it doesn't make for a great game.Also there was a man floating in the middle of the road. Yay bugs! So far I've seen objects that can't be picked up, people walking through closed elevator doors, wall glitches and places to fall through the map, calling cars only for them to fall out of the sky, floating cans, chopsticks, etc. This is fairly noticeable stuff that should have been fixed earlier, but probably will be in later patches because it breaks the fourth wall too often and borders on Bethesda RPG-like glitching - but it provides comic-relief in an otherwise straight take.One other aspect is the remote hacking done on you. "Overheat" in particular is going to drive players up the wall. In many ways all the quickhacking in the game is overwhelming at first. It takes some getting used to. The other annoying thing? Electricity weapons which will kill you in one shot. Frustration city here we come.The music on radio bolsters the atmosphere. Unfortunately it is not particularly remarkable, except for one Japanese kawaii-decora styled track which had me in stitches because I understood the perverted Japanese lyrics! Pity the rest of what passes for music in 2077 is industrial trash - but given the world's current trajectory - it's probably accurate. A good opportunity to add in more synthwave and vapourwave went begging, with a touch of Japanese 80's funk would have made it better.Beyond this, it all gets problematic in the story. The pacing is... er... not so great. 10 hours in and apparently I haven't even really started the story. For the first few hours you have no idea who you are, what you're doing, or what world you are even inhabiting. It feels like I'm missing an amazing amount of backstory, and I'm not sure if I have the patience to read all the notes dropped around the world to make sense of it. Also the prologue feels very linear - which I suppose is to be expected for what amounts to a glorified tutorial. I'm just struggling to wonder if or why I should care about this world.The other elephant in the room is the lack of multiplayer - although this itself is a huge ask given what's already been produced as an RPG. It's inclusion would have boosted this game into another level - where Call of Duty style deathmatches and battle-royale could have worked rather seamlessly. Unfortunately it is absent, but one can certainly see the potential.If you're playing this game, you are here for the amazing graphics, the vibe, and possibly the story. The game, not so much. The potential was there for some epic gameplay, but the execution is a bit meh. Shame. I appreciate what the developers have tried to do here and they have succeeded on one front: the RED engine is something to behold - when they fix the bugs. Perhaps with some decent writing, pacing, and improved gameplay - the next CD Projekt RED game will be a real winner and GTA V might have some real competition. Might have to wait until 2077 though, but we'll all have better graphics cards by then.

Well, where do I begin?5hours in; Mediocre over-hyped Open World RPG. Clearly a rushed decision to release early. Definitely needs more work. Good story and heavy on narration but the gameplay sucks. NPC AI is buggy / nonexistent and for it being such an intense world and it feels rather lifeless. At the time of my review I'd played this game for 90 minutes. My review 90mins in; - They couldn't even release it on time (Even at 00:00 it wasn't playable until 00:20+)- They delayed multiple times (Partially thanks to the pandemic)- Even after release the game still feels unpolished and is really buggy- The start of the game is very boring and gives you little to no feel for how the actual game will be- Feels like it was made by Bethesda instead of CDPR- Chrome and Gold reflective textures dont do this games graphics justice- Character customisation is 'complex' but also limited? It gives you many options, but the options don't have many options. Lip stick colour for example is very limited. (Apparently more options will come in the future?)- Texture work even on things that should be obvious (The ground for example) are terrible. Max settings looks similar to GTA 5. (Texture streaming bugs apparently, even though I play on a Samsung 970 Plus NVMe SSD)- Doesn't do a great job of letting you know you've just taken a bullet, I didn't notice how low my health was until I bothered to look at my health bar. No hit indicator, no jam, no feedback (Is a bug, requires reloading the game save)- NPC likes to stand directly in front of you so you can't shoot (Generally buggy / lackluster AI awareness)- You cannot change Anti-Aliasing technique and the one it uses makes things blurry / soft and I hate it. MFAA I believe. Give me FXAA OR NOTHING! (TAA is forced and cannot be disabled. However Nvidia overlay works to sharpen things up)- Graphics options don't have much effect on performance. DLSS does though.- You cannot rebind things that should be able to be rebound. For example, the F key (interact). Apparently this will be fixed in the future.Positives;- The world is open, really cool and lots to do. However it all seems a little boring and lifeless. Hopefully this will be better when they improve the NPC AI.- Feels like Division 2 in terms of how spongy the enemies are (Depends on difficulty I guess, I played on Very Hard but switched to Hard, seems better now)- The sound stage is excellent. Audio is very crisp and directional audio is great as well.Overall so far? 5.4/10. Just about passable only because I know CDPR will work out the bugs in the future but for now, avoid this title.I'll update if I change my mind but so far this game needs work. This is either Cyberpunk 2077 but it's just not finished. This does not feel like a game of the same quality that Witcher 3 managed to achieve. I hope the story is good but I'm yet to complete the game and do anything rememberable.Edit: To respond to those people berating me because of my playtime or choice of FXAA - FXAA still shows jagged edges and has the least smearing out of all of the AA options (if there were any lol) and I understand 1.4 hours probably isn't enough to review the actual game story itself which is why I didn't say much for it. This review is mostly for the state of the game NOT a review for the story. However to counter that, 90 minutes into the game I found myself quite bored. This feels a rushed release. The fact you cannot change some of the keybindings or anti-aliasing options makes me believe so. It is missing options every PC game should have.Edit 2: Tried to play the game again today and the REDlauncher crashed as I was signing up for extra in-game loot... Off to a great start. (probably due to millions playing the game)Edit 3: To clarify, all my drivers are the latest they can be. I'm running the game on an Intel Core i9 9900K, 32GB RAM and a RTX 2080 Ti. Next-gen graphical disappointment and dystopian junkyard fire.Second time around playing this game and I am literally getting depressed AF.CampaignThe game demonstrates a dystopian transhumanist future whereby implants are all the rage, and you're left with a concrete abortion of a jungle posing as a futuristic city. While some praise this game for its futurescape, the absolutely plastic fake superficial world presented is enough to warrant a prescription for antidepressants, much less the adoption of a new drug habit. After a while, meandering around in this technological refuse bin of a city, the repetitive motion of eyes glazed over NPCs stumbling around aimlessly or huddled in some corner, drug addled messes, is enough for me to scream and close this game.5 hours in and I've heard plenty of dialogue, I've followed around some big dude, I've accepted jobs here and there but I haven't done anything incredible yet or amazing.One notable event was when you rescue the woman found in the bathtub in ice. When you bring her outside, the armed medivac pulling in out of nowhere was pretty cool. Other than that, from a story point of view, the game play has been bland, if anything. Some of the best RPGs out there- Fallout 3 and Fallout NV - have set the bar high. The game doesn't offer that much of an array of choices when it comes to interacting with characters.The gunplay is as you would find any other game and I'm not really a fan of the hit points. I find the NPCs in the city to be uninspiring - the majority of them seem to carry on like strung out junkies, not doing much and holding their head in their hands. While I find the landscapes and buildings graphically well-done, the people who fill it don't add substance to the overall picture. In all honesty,  the game plays like a ray-tracing demo . After having played open-world games like Mafia 2 and 3 and Assassin's creed, along with Hitman 2, where these devs have mastered the concepts of large, populated open world games with vibrant people, I find Cyberpunk's contribution to this to be underwhelming, even more when you consider the hype.If the depressing futuristic version of life in this game isn't enough to make me want to slit my wrists, the absolute banality and tedium of conversations with NPCs is a surefire way of making me want to casually walk into highway traffic. With some NPCs on a mission quest, you are literally 5 minutes listening to some half cyborg half human prattle on. 20 minutes later I'm literally wondering how much more I can tolerate of this. You then realize that the game is a bloated mess - graphically and conversationally. If the futurism here isn't depressing enough, the abject lack of anything remotely substantive in the game itself from one mission to the next is a flatline for me. VisuallyVisually the ray-tracing effects are beautiful.The future dystopian landscapes are visually amazing, the reflections are downright incredible. The peripheral aspects of this game demonstrate I think one of the developers' biggest strengths. Walking down the street, having your senses assaulted by the Japanese audio clips, the random soundbites of passing NPCs, the lights and the sounds make this visually a powerhouse. However the models themselves of NPCsI find pale in comparison with the geometry of the city. Lip syncing is way off, and some characters look downright plastic in the light.The steam reviews are a toxic dumping ground of immature fan boys who simply shout down other people who complain about performance issues due tot heir pc specs. For a more accurate and less idiotic group of reviews, check out the forums on GOG.At this point, charging 80$ for this game hasn't justified itself. Hearing that the game spent nearly a decade in development, this borders on disappointment, especially with the hype, AND CD projekt's stellar job with the Witcher series.Verdict: the game is as empty and as bankrupt as its depiction of the future. You need a super computer to run this thing on ultra, much like you need a Xanax or Adderall to help you stomach the tedium.

Despite the current "very positive" reviews on Steam, I'd like to remember you all the absolute dumpster that was this game at launch and for years after, as some seem to be a bit too quick to go back to licking the boots of their favorite corpo overlords. The many promises that CDPR failed to deliver on and how they mislead their customers. Here’s a quick breakdown of some of the features we were told to expect but were missing or poorly implemented, some even to date:- AI Systems: We were promised an amazing AI that would govern NPCs' daily lives and combat behaviors. Instead, we have simplistic and often broken AI that fails to live up to the hype.- Wanted System and Corrupt Police: The game's wanted system is basic, with the police often spawning out of nowhere, lacking the depth of a corrupt police force or varying law enforcement reactions based on the crime location.- Combat and Hacking: While some combat and hacking features exist, the promised depth and variety, like hacking with the nanowire or uploading complex viruses, are sorely missing. The system quickly becomes repetitive.- Immersion and World Interactivity: Key immersive features such as a meaningful trauma team, flying AVs, targeted ads, and a dynamic marketplace are absent. These omissions significantly detract from the world-building that was promised.- Strong RPG Elements: CDPR claimed, just four months before release, that Cyberpunk 2077 would be a much deeper roleplaying experience than The Witcher 3. However, the game lacks strong RPG elements, such as meaningful skill checks, complex companions, and impactful faction dynamics. What we have is more of a shooter/looter with stats rather than a deep role-playing experience. It's telling that the game was reclassified as an "open-world, action-adventure story" on their official page right before release, which feels scummy and misleading.- NPC Routines and AI: The promised unique daily routines for NPCs are nowhere to be found, making the world feel static and lifeless.- Quest Relevance and Decisions: Quest decisions were supposed to have a significant impact on the world, but this feature is barely noticeable in the final game.- Day and Night Cycle: The day and night cycle is mostly cosmetic and doesn't influence gameplay in any meaningful way. Venues are always open, and there's no noticeable change in danger levels at night.- Character Customization: Despite the hype, the character customization is underwhelming and lacks the promised depth during creation and in-game.- Drone Usage: Drones were supposed to play a significant role in the game, but they are limited to just a few missions.- Lifepaths and Non-linear Quests: Lifepaths barely impact the storyline, leading to a linear quest design that contradicts the non-linear experience that was advertised.- Special Abilities: Nanowire and gorilla arms were supposed to have multiple uses, yet their functionality is very limited in the actual game.- Performance: On Last-gen Consoles the game ran poorly, contradicting CDPR's claims that it would run smoothly. Was also bad on PC, but i guess at least they never said it would run well on PC? LOL- Release Readiness: CDPR claimed the game would launch "when it's ready," but the state of the game at release proved otherwise.- Braindance Variety: The braindance mechanic is underutilized and far less interactive than what was implied.- Challenging Weather System: Promises of a weather system that impacts gameplay, like acid rain, were not fulfilled.- Romance and Relationship Options: The romance options are minimal and do not reflect the deep relationships that were promised.- Game Completion without Main Quest: It’s not possible to finish the game through side quests alone, contrary to what was claimed.- Gender and Body Customization: The freedom to mix and match voice, gender, and body type is less flexible than promised.- Polished Experience: The game was far from polished at launch, filled with bugs and performance issues.- Weapon Customization: Weapon customization is limited, despite promises of extensive options.- NPC Reactions to Styles: The promised NPC reactions to the player’s style choices are almost nonexistent.- Features that were transparently removed during development include property customization, a transportation system, wall running, vehicle customization, and voice customization beyond gender choice.Remember that launch! While some of these issues have been fixed, we should never forget what CDPR did. They misled and disappointed millions of players. We should learn from this experience and hold these greedy corporations accountable for their promises."♥♥♥♥ corpos"
